```{r}
#| include: false
#| eval: !expr has_data
p <- results$primary
adj <- results$adjusted
covariate_labels <- c(
  age = "age", bmi = "BMI", sex = "sex", asa = "ASA physical status",
  smoking = "smoking", surgery_size = "surgery size",
  preop_sore_throat = "sore throat before surgery"
)
adj_covariates <- covariate_labels[strsplit(adj$covariates, ", ")[[1]]]
```

The primary question is whether a licorice gargle, compared with a
sugar-water gargle, lowers the odds of any sore throat at rest thirty
minutes after arrival in the recovery room. "Any" means a score above zero
on the zero-to-ten scale (D-001). Every comparison below is licorice
against sugar water, in the patients observed at thirty minutes.

## The simplest answer

`r if (has_data) sprintf("Thirty minutes after arrival in the recovery room, %s patients in the sugar-water arm had a sore throat at rest, compared with %s in the licorice arm.", fmt_prop(p$p_sugar, p$n_sugar), fmt_prop(p$p_licorice, p$n_licorice)) else ""`
`r if (has_data) sprintf("The risk difference is %s.", fmt_rd(p)) else ""`

## Primary model: the marginal odds ratio

The pre-specified primary model is an unadjusted logistic regression of
any sore throat on treatment (Chapter 3; D-007). With treatment as its
only term, its odds ratio is the population-averaged (marginal) odds
ratio. It compares the odds of sore throat had every patient gargled
licorice with the odds had every patient gargled sugar water.

`r if (has_data) sprintf("The marginal odds ratio is %s (%s, %d patients).", fmt_or(p), fmt_p(p$p_value), p$n_obs) else ""`
Because sore throat is common, the odds ratio is further from one than
the ratio of the two proportions, so the risk difference above is the
easier number to read (D-006).

Patients missing the primary outcome cannot change this conclusion: the
best- and worst-case bounds both keep the confidence interval below one
(Chapter 2).

## Sensitivity analysis: adjusted for baseline covariates

The plan adjusts for baseline covariates as a sensitivity analysis only
(D-009, D-011). The covariates are listed below. Age and BMI enter as
linear terms, and the rest as factors.

`r if (has_data) sprintf("Covariates in the model: %s.", paste(adj_covariates, collapse = ", ")) else ""`
`r if (has_data) sprintf("The covariate-adjusted odds ratio is %s (%s, %d patients).", fmt_or(adj), fmt_p(adj$p_value), adj$n_obs) else ""`

This is a **conditional** odds ratio. It compares patients with the same
covariate values, not the whole population. Odds ratios are
non-collapsible, so the adjusted odds ratio differs from the unadjusted
one even when the arms are perfectly balanced. A difference between the
two is not evidence of confounding (D-009). The two estimates agree in
direction and their confidence intervals overlap almost entirely.
